claims.text: Terraform and OpenTofu can use a self-hosted Pulumi Cloud instance as a state backend by setting an environment variable on the API service.
The state backend guide is located at /docs/integrations/terraform/state-backend/.
The PULUMI_TFE_DOMAIN environment variable sets the domain that serves the Terraform-compatible API on the Pulumi self-hosted API service.
When PULUMI_TFE_DOMAIN is unset, the Terraform-compatible API on the self-hosted Pulumi API service is disabled and its routes aren't registered.
The DNS record for the PULUMI_TFE_DOMAIN domain should point at the same host that serves the PULUMI_API_DOMAIN.
Using a separate domain for PULUMI_TFE_DOMAIN keeps the Terraform-compatible API distinct from the Pulumi API, but a separate domain is not required.
PULUMI_TFE_DOMAIN can be set to the same value as PULUMI_API_DOMAIN if a second DNS record is not desired.

In Terraform or OpenTofu configuration, the terraform login or tofu login command, and the TF_TOKEN_* variable name should use the PULUMI_TFE_DOMAIN value wherever the state backend guide uses tf.pulumi.com.
The state backend guide at /docs/integrations/terraform/state-backend/ uses tf.pulumi.com as an example domain.
